'''''Animal Math''''' is an educational book series featuring baby animals that introduces reader to mathematic principles. The series consists of five books: ''Tiger Math'' (2000), ''Chimp Math'' (2002), ''Polar Bear Math'' (2004), ''Panda Math'' (2005), and ''Cheetah Math'' (2007). On the right-hand pages, the books tell stories of baby animals cared for at either the [[Denver Zoo]] or [[San Diego Zoo]] who needed extra care when they were young. The left-hand pages discuss basic mathematic concepts using the animals as examples in problems.

Published by [[Henry Holt and Company]], the books are authored by Ann Whitehead Nagda, with support from Cindy Bickel, an assistant at the Denver Zoo, or in collaboration with the San Diego Zoo.

== Books ==

=== ''Tiger Math'' (2000) ===
''Tiger Math: Learning to Graph from a Baby Tiger'' (2000), co-written by Ann Whitehead Nagda and Cindy Bickel, teaches students about different types of graphs, including [[bar graph]]s, [[line graph]]s, picture graphs, and [[pie charts]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Phelan |first=Carolyn |date=2000-10-01 |title=Tiger Math |url=https://www.booklistonline.com/products/642987 |url-access=subscription |access-date=2025-11-20 |website=[[Booklist]]}}</ref> The book features the [[Siberian tiger]] cub T. J., who was born at the Denver Zoo, then struggled to eat after his mother died.<ref name=":2">{{Cite web |date=2000-07-01 |title=Tiger Math |url=https://www.kirkusreviews.com/book-reviews/ann-whitehead-nagda/tiger-math/ |access-date=2025-11-20 |website=[[Kirkus Reviews]]}}</ref>

''Tiger Math'' is a [[Junior Library Guild]] book.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Tiger Math |url=https://www.juniorlibraryguild.com/tiger-math-9780805062489j |access-date=2025-11-20 |website=[[Junior Library Guild]] |language=en}}</ref> ''Kirkus Reviews'' said the book provided "a delightful way to learn math".<ref name=":2" />

=== ''Chimp Math'' (2002) ===
''Chimp Math: Learning about Time from a Baby Chimpanzee'' (2002), co-written by Ann Whitehead Nagda and Cindy Bickel,  teaches students about time, such as timelines and telling time on a clock.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2002-11-01 |title=Chimp Math: Learning about TIme from a Baby Chimpanzee. |url=https://www.booklistonline.com/products/1122251 |url-access=subscription |access-date=2025-11-20 |website=[[Booklist]]}}</ref> The book features Jiggs, a baby [[chimpanzee]] at the Denver Zoo who was ignored by his mother. Jiggs is kept in the zoo's nursery during the day and stays with Bickel in the evenings. While in the nursery, he spends time with a [[jaguar]] cub named Giorgio, before returning to the chimpanzee enclosure.<ref name=":3">{{Cite web |date=2002-10-15 |title=Chimp Math |url=https://www.kirkusreviews.com/book-reviews/ann-whitehead-nagda/chimp-math/ |access-date=2025-11-20 |website=[[Kirkus Reviews]]}}</ref>

''Kirkus Reviews'' praised ''Chimp Math'', highlighting her strength of "combining multiple disciplines and teaching in a non-threatening, as-you-need-it manner".<ref name=":3" />

=== ''Polar Bear Math'' (2004) ===
''Polar Bear Math: Learning about Fractions from Klondike and Snow'' (2004), co-written by Ann Whitehead Nagda and Cindy Bickel, teaches students about [[fractions]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=2004-09-01 |title=Polar Bear Math: Learning About Fractions from Klondike and Snow |url=https://www.booklistonline.com/products/1162196 |url-access=subscription |access-date=2024-11-20 |website=[[Booklist]]}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last1=Ison |first1=Alyssa |last2=Pham |first2=Jonathan |date=2008-08-17 |title=Learning math |url=https://www.newspapers.com/image-view/730521181/?match=1&terms=%22Cheetah%20Math%22 |access-date=2025-11-20 |website=[[Newsday]] |language=en-US |via=[[Newspapers.com]]}}</ref> The book features the polar bear cubs Klondike and Snow, who were cared for at the [[Denver Zoo Conservation Alliance|Denver Zoo]] after being abandoned. Along with a vet and another assistant at the zoo, Bickel learns how to care for the polar bears, who eventually thrive.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2004-07-15 |title=Polar Bear Math |url=https://www.kirkusreviews.com/book-reviews/ann-whitehead-nagda/polar-bear-math/ |access-date=2025-11-20 |website=[[Kirkus Reviews]]}}</ref>

''Polar Bear Math'' is a Junior Library Guild book.<ref name=":1">{{Cite web |title=Polar Bear Math |url=https://www.juniorlibraryguild.com/polar-bear-math-9780805073010j |access-date=2025-11-20 |website=[[Junior Library Guild]] |language=en}}</ref>

=== ''Panda Math'' (2005) ===
''Panda Math: Learning about Subtraction from Hua Mei and Mei Sheng'' (2005), written by Ann Whitehead Nagda in collaboration with the [[San Diego Zoo]], teaches students about [[subtraction]]. The mathematical text discusses different ways to subtract,<ref>{{Cite web |date=2008-01-12 |title=Mathematics can be fun |url=https://www.newspapers.com/image/734751993/ |access-date=2025-11-20 |website=[[North Bay Nugget]] |page=B2 |language=en-US |via=Newspapers.com}}</ref> including "regrouping, subtracting each place value, thinking about doubles and adding up".''<ref name=":4">{{Cite web |date=2005-07-15 |title=Panda Math |url=https://www.kirkusreviews.com/book-reviews/ann-whitehead-nagda/panda-math/ |access-date=2025-11-20 |website=[[Kirkus Reviews]]}}</ref>'' The story features  Hua Mei and Mei Sheng, panda cubs at the San Diego Zoo.''<ref name=":4" />''

According to ''[[Kirkus Reviews]]'', Nagda explains the different approaches to solving subtraction problems well, though they concede that "children will need additional support".''<ref name=":4" />''

=== ''Cheetah Math'' (2007) ===
''Cheetah Math: Learning about Division from Baby Cheetahs'' (2007), written by Ann Whitehead Nagda in collaboration with the [[San Diego Zoo]], teaches students about [[Division (mathematics)|division]]. The book features the baby [[cheetah]]s Majani and Kubali, who were raised at the San Diego Zoo.<ref name=":0">{{Cite web |date=2023-02-24 |title=Cheetah Math |url=https://www.kirkusreviews.com/book-reviews/ann-whitehead-nagda/cheetah-math/ |access-date=2025-11-20 |website=[[Kirkus Reviews]]}}</ref>

''Cheetah Math'' is a Junior Library Guild book.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Cheetah Math: Learning about Division from Baby Cheetahs |url=https://www.juniorlibraryguild.com/cheetah-math-learning-about-division-fro-9780805076455j |access-date=2025-11-20 |website=[[Junior Library Guild]] |language=en}}</ref> Sally Woolsey called the book "well done" and it is a popular item in many elementary school libraries.{{Citation needed|date=November 2025}} ''[[Kirkus Reviews]]'' called the book "a great addition to both the math and wild-animal conservation bookshelves".<ref name=":0" /> The ''[[School Library Journal]]'' also gave a favorable review, saying ''Cheetah Math'' "is a wonderful cross-curricular book and an appealing way to introduce math".<ref name="Author">{{Cite web |title=Author's website |url=http://www.annnagda.com/CheetahMath.htm |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20080725164731/http://www.annnagda.com/CheetahMath.htm |archive-date=2008-07-25 |access-date=2008-09-26}}</ref>
